newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Danu, Finance One merger now takeover.
newsitem.headline: Thai Danu, Finance One merger now takeover.

text.p: The biggest planned merger of two Thai financial institutions turned into a takeover on Tuesday after Thai Danu Bank decided to acquire Finance One, central banker Rerngchai Marakanond said.
"They have changed from merger to acquisition because their earlier plans of merging company A with company B had run into a relatively large number of problems," Rergnchai told reporters.
Last week Thai Danu Bank denied rumours it had decided to take over cash-strapped Finance One instead of merging with the company that was once Thailand's largest finance firm.
The bank said on Friday the due diligence process had gone too far to make a change and the company boards were due to hold meetings on Thursday to vote on the merger.
Rergnchai did not disclose a deadline for the new takeover plan, but said: "We have given them a timeframe and they should come up with some progress by next week.
Central bank officials were quoted by local media last week as saying the central bank preferred a takeover to a merger if it could speed up the rescue of Finance One.
The comments followed rumours that Thai Danu was planning to walk away from the merger due to various problems.
Analysts said due diligence -- which took two weeks longer than originally planned -- probably exposed Finance One's weak financial position.
The analysts had said earlier that Thai Danu's shareholders were not expected to approve a merger once the extent of Finance One's problems were known.

Analysts said Finance One sought the merger -- which would have been the largest between two Thai financial institutions -- because it faced liquidity problems that emerged during a major shakeup of Thailand's troubled finance sector.

Under the terms of the merger, Thai Danu had planned to take six billion baht ($231 million) of Finance One's property loans. Finance One has a total of 66 billion baht in outstanding loans -- 20 billion of which are in the property sector.
The merger plan between Thai Danu and Finance One set in motion proposed mergers between several of Thailand's troubled finance and securities companies.

Analysts said the process was just the start of a shake-up among the country's 91 finance and securities firms. The industry is suffering from declining loan portfolio quality, high financing costs and losses due to the depressed bourse.
Rergnchai told a seminar on mergers of finance firms that the government would give generous incentives to finance companies that planned to merge.
The incentives would allow the companies to do foreign exchange business and retail banking. Most finance companies are currently not licenced to undertake these businesses.
"This is a golden opportunity for finance companies to merge," Rergnchai said. "They can choose either to be big department stores or remain as small boutique shops." ($1 = 26 baht)
